primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.edition: Springer 2007, reprint of the corrected 1994 edition
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Antecedent for distributional realization of prescribed limits of broken rays. The independent proof expands the controlled smooth families, changing-section orders, complete countable test space, Baire argument and exact endpoint wavefronts.

source_correspondence: T0 retains a scalar smooth real quadratic principal symbol, noncharacteristic face, arbitrary complex lower coefficients, positively normalized uniform limits of finite transverse broken rays, injective target cosphere image and interior endpoints. The approximating ordinary rays have nonzero Hamilton base velocity. The conclusion is a continuous compactly supported intrinsic distribution with zero actual Dirichlet value and exact solution and forcing wavefronts.

T1 proves eventual injectivity using uniqueness only on the ordinary and transverse reflected approximants. A normalized return makes the approximating orbit periodic. Uniform convergence and target injectivity make the return interval shrink; equicontinuity makes its entire periodic image shrink, contradicting the nonconstant target.

T2 uses the exact Gaussian threshold at s=n+4, a fixed compact localization and frequency regularization with uniform order-zero symbol bounds. The full finite broken-ray chain pairs identical complete traces at every reflection. The Cauchy kernel has order minus one quarter and restriction to a transverse output section adds one quarter, giving graph order zero without excess. Consequently increasing the number of reflections changes constants but not the fixed Sobolev order.

T2 differentiates the full section family and uses compact parameter integration to control the joint H^{s-1} norm and hence the supremum norm. All graph, factorization and partition defects are smoothing operators on the same bounded datum, uniformly with every normal jet. Only finitely many prescribed good tests need control; interior endpoint caps can avoid all their microsupports.

T2 critical failure is checked in the seed canonical chart using the complete inverse graph and the earlier SP:S4 constant-factor Sobolev criterion. Distributional convergence and the Fourier bounded-norm limit argument then force the smooth family critical Hs norms to be unbounded. The proof does not infer joint Hs regularity from an ordinary trace estimate with a half-order loss.

T3 defines an explicit countable family of forcing, interior solution and tangential boundary tests, with proper support and rational compact/conic exhaustions. Smooth forcing on a whole boundary neighborhood supplies the noncharacteristic intrinsic extension. The actual trace agrees with the continuous value by normal recovery and the approximate-delta limit. Continuity alone is not asserted to imply intrinsic membership.

T4 proves completeness by uniform convergence, continuity of actual transposed proper operators, uniform derivative limits and the fundamental theorem of calculus. The limiting noncharacteristic equation supplies the same intrinsic domain and zero trace, without assigning an unspecified topology to that domain.

T5 derives the finite-seminorm estimate directly from the proved complete-metric Baire theorem. Fixed compact output support gives pointwise Fourier convergence; Fatou makes each Sobolev norm ball closed. Subtraction and scaling inside the open seminorm ball give the precise coefficient 4m/delta.

T6 uses a microlocal interior test separated from the two endpoint states. It allows repeated endpoint base projections and vanishing limiting Hamilton base velocity. Uniform convergence separates a sufficiently late approximating ray from the finite list of good tests. One fixed smooth family then has bounded defining seminorms and unbounded tested critical norm, contradicting the Baire estimate.

T7 excludes stationary ordinary or nondiffractive gliding states on an injective limit. At third-order contact the exact comparison forcing stays zero on the radial gliding orbit by homogeneity, so the generalized curve is its constant normalized orbit. At nonradial glancing a common tangential clock and embedded target make the contained two-sided singular arc contain an open target interval. This does not require uniqueness among curves outside the target at infinite contact.

T8 uses ordinary interior propagation across each endpoint. The exterior continuation is outside the embedded target and regular; a regular forcing covector at either endpoint would contradict the already singular target interior. Both endpoint forcing rays are therefore necessary.

The three complete solutions prove exact compressed strip convergence, the finite Baire scaling constant and a uniformly lower-order frequency family with logarithmically divergent critical norm. The original two-panel figure retains the exact normal position, compressed normal momentum, time orientation, wall hits and endpoint positions; it illustrates a transverse limiting family, not an asserted glancing example.
All 186 formulas and 23 displays parse, and every mobile display and figure extent is accessible. Seventy-four exact algebraic model checks pass; these finite checks accompany the analytic proof.
